Opportunity summary: Embercliff (mid-tier enterprise fintech) evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private plan for customer-facing chat, fraud signal reranking, and embeddings-backed search. Very sticky data residency + audit needs; exploring on-prem gateway for high-sensitivity flows.

Sales history / timeline (mutable):

- 2026-02-02: discovery call — discussed architectural options: Dedicated GPU pools + VPC, optional air-gapped staging. (notes: "we cannot send raw PII off-network for reconciliation")

Key technical requirements / acceptance criteria:
- Workloads: chat (customer support assistant) steady-state QPS target 80, peak bursts to 400+. reranking pipeline ~200 qps (short prompts), embeddings upsert throughput during off-peak windows.
- Latency SLOs: P50 < 40ms (local routing), P90 < 120ms for chat; P99 < 300ms acceptable with fallback policy. Reranker target P90 < 80ms.
- Throughput guarantees: require reserved GPU capacity for sustained 2000 tokens/sec aggregate across 8-hour business window; peak token/sec up to 10k/sec for flash events.
- Fault tolerance: automatic fallback to smaller quantized model in event of capacity shortage, but must preserve hallucination bounds for financial domain.
- Security/compliance: on-prem or VPC private control plane; HSM-backed KMS for signing; audit logs retention 7 years for regulated flows; SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning.

Sizing workshop outputs (what Redwood delivered):
- Baseline throughput matrix: model variant (base, 8-bit q, 4-bit q) vs tokens/sec per GPU, observed latencies at 128/256/512 seq lengths. (workshop artifact: /drive/embercliff/dedicated-sizing-workshop-v1.pdf)
- Recommended reserved pool: 12x A100-style 80GB equivalents (or cloud-equivalent units) to meet steady-state + 2x buffer for failover, with autoscale headroom for bursts. Rationale: measured steady token/sec 2.4k per GPU with our kernel and batching; business window needs 2k sustained.
- Suggested SLO commitments for contract: guaranteed sustained throughput (2k tokens/sec) with credits for breaches, P99 latency target 300ms for 99.9% uptime SLA, maintenance windows restricted to off-hours.
- Cost/perf tuning: enable KV prefix caching for chat sessions to cut token regen 23% on average; batching policy to prioritize low-latency traffic on separate lanes.

- Legal: draft SLA language on throughput credits — Embercliff wants explicit credits for crediting overage if baseline not met; Redwood legal needs to confirm measurable metric definitions.
- KMS: Embercliff may require on-prem HSM integration (partner vendor). SE needs to validate Redwood Private KMS connector compatibility.
- Budget: procurement committee wants two pricing scenarios: committed monthly vs blended on-demand + burst. Need TCO over 12/24 months.
- Model residency: certain PII flows must remain on-prem; policy routing required (smart routing + model variants). Implementation complexity could push timeline by 6-8 weeks.
